description: Renovate runs on more than one GitLab pipeline schedule here, and the `schedule` window below is what makes that safe (#243). The Monday window is the only time new update MRs may be opened; the other runs exist to finish an automerge that was lost when its MR was created. Delete the window and every one of those runs starts opening MRs of its own, up to `prConcurrentLimit`.

Why a second cadence is needed at all: Renovate's GitLab platform arms platform-native automerge exactly once, from `createPr`, and re-arms only on a run that pushes a new commit to the branch — so an arming attempt lost at creation is never retried by itself, and it fails silently (see `logLevelRemap`). What does recover it is Renovate's own automerge, the fallback the docs promise for when native automerge is unavailable: on a later run where the branch is unchanged, Renovate merges the MR itself once the branch status is green, and that path is reachable outside `schedule` because an existing branch plus MR falls through the schedule gate to 'will update if necessary'. A weekly cadence left that recovery seven days away, which is why five MRs opened on 2026-08-10 sat unmerged until they were merged by hand.

Keep the minute field of any cron window as `*`: Renovate has no minute granularity and rejects anything else, so the pipeline schedule's own cron (`0 7 * * 1`) is the one string not to paste here. Widen the window if the Monday run starts missing it — the docs ask for a 3-4 hour window unless Renovate runs more often than that, which here it does. `src/lib/renovate-hygiene.test.ts` asserts that the window exists and that its minute field is a wildcard, because nothing in CI runs renovate-config-validator.

logLevelRemap.description: Make a failed automerge arming attempt visible. Every failure inside Renovate's `tryPrAutomerge` is logged at `debug` and swallowed, and this job runs at `info` — so five MRs that never armed automerge produced no output at all, anywhere, and the cause took a day to find (#243). `warn` is the level that reaches a person rather than a log file: Renovate registers its problems stream at `warn`, and the Dependency Dashboard reprints whatever lands there under a '## Repository Problems' heading, so the next lost attempt appears on #17 instead of only in a job nobody opens. Raising the whole job to `LOG_LEVEL=debug` was the alternative and is worse — tens of MB of log per run with this one line buried in it, which is a different way of being invisible. The `/…/` regex form is used rather than a glob because `src/lib/renovate-hygiene.ts` reads that form when it asserts this entry still exists; both of Renovate's two wordings for this failure are covered by the prefix.

customManagers.description: Track the pinned image refs in the Helm chart values.yaml (postgres server — which the backup dumpImage also inherits — and the backup upload image google/cloud-sdk). These are single-string `name:tag@digest` values, not the repository/tag shape the built-in helm-values manager parses, so an annotated regex manager is used instead. Add a `# renovate: datasource=docker depName=<image> [versioning=docker]` line directly above any new image field to bring it under tracking (#15).

packageRules.description: Automerge patch/minor/digest/pin once the MR pipeline passes. The pipeline runs all scanners as REQUIRED jobs on MRs (they must execute), and new Critical/High findings are blocked by the Scan Result Policy (issue #2, task 4.2) — enable that policy before turning the Renovate schedule on. Majors always need manual review + Duo.
Group and label the Docker/CI base-image (node:22-alpine) bumps together.

Keep react and react-dom in a single MR - splitting them produces two MRs that can never merge. React 19 asserts at runtime that the two packages are the exact same version (https://react.dev/warnings/version-mismatch), so a react-only bump breaks: !146 (react 19.2.8, react-dom 19.2.7) passed dependency resolution and then failed 47 test files with 'Incompatible React versions'. A react-dom-only bump is not even resolvable, because react-dom@X peers react ^X against our exact pin: npm exits ERESOLVE, Renovate's updateArtifacts step fails, and the MR lands with a bumped package.json and no lockfile change at all (!147). Grouping makes the peer pair move together. @types/react and @types/react-dom are in the group for a weaker but real version of the same reason (!148 review): @types/react-dom@19.2.3 peers @types/react ^19.2.0, a minor-pinned range, so once DefinitelyTyped ships @types/react-dom@19.3.x it will peer ^19.3.0 and ERESOLVE against a 19.2.x @types/react exactly like the runtime pair did. Remove this rule only once react/react-dom stop being release-locked peers, or if this repo stops exact-pinning them.

Keep tsx on a release whose esbuild range overlaps vite's, so the lockfile resolves esbuild to a SINGLE version (#67). Renovate regenerates lockfiles with npm 11 while CI installs with npm 10 (node:22-alpine). When tsx 4.19.2 pinned esbuild ~0.23.0 and vitest's nested vite 8 needed ^0.28, npm nested a second esbuild subtree — and npm 11 dropped those 28 entries while keeping the nested vite that required them, producing a lockfile CI's npm ci rejected as out of sync. That blocked every dependency MR (!143/!146/!147) until each lockfile was rebuilt by hand. tsx >= 4.22.0 moved to esbuild ~0.28.0, which overlaps vite 8, so there is no nested subtree left for either npm version to disagree about. The invariant is enforced by src/lib/lockfile-hygiene.test.ts — if that test fails, realign the ranges rather than deleting it.

Defer ESLint 10 (#21/!51): no released eslint-plugin-react supports it (latest 7.37.5 peers eslint ^3||...||^9.7, pinned via eslint-config-next). Lift this line once the Next plugin chain ships ESLint-10 support - Renovate will re-propose the major automatically.

Defer TypeScript 7 (!68): TS 7 is the Go-native compiler; @typescript-eslint 8.62.1 peers typescript >=4.8.4 <6.1.0 (via eslint-config-next), so typescript-estree crashes at module load and lint/build fail. The <6.1 ceiling matches that peer range and still lets Renovate propose TS 6.0.x (the JS-based sibling release). This cap also applies to vulnerabilityAlerts MRs (Renovate does not auto-bypass allowedVersions for security fixes) - accepted trade-off: typescript is a devDependency (never in the runtime bundle), TS itself rarely carries CVEs, and a TS-7-only fix would crash this same lint toolchain regardless, so the real remediation is lifting this defer. Lift this line once the typescript-eslint chain ships TS-7 support - Renovate will re-propose the major automatically.

Keep the TOP-LEVEL brace-expansion override on the patched 5.x line (#161/#82). CVE-2026-14257 / GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg widened to cover 2.x and there is no patched 2.x/3.x/4.x backport, so 5.0.8 is the floor. !245 - titled 'update dependency brace-expansion to v2.1.4' - rewrote this entry to ^2.1.3, back inside the affected range. It was classified `patch`, so the automerge rule at the top of this list applied to it; only an unresolved review discussion stopped it merging unattended, and the scan-result policy did not object because the head pipeline's security summary was identical to main's. The cause is a lockedVersion mis-resolution, not a one-off: Renovate reads this entry's current version from the HOISTED node_modules/brace-expansion, which the nested minimatch@^3 override below pins to 2.1.3, whereas the copy this entry actually governs is nested under @ts-morph/common (shadcn -> ts-morph) and is the only production-reachable one. Renovate therefore sees this entry as 'currently 2.1.3' and offers 2.1.3 -> 2.1.4 as a patch, writing the range it derived from that reading over the deliberate ^5.0.8 - and it will do so again on every future 2.x release. The floor makes those releases ineligible while leaving the wanted direction open: 5.0.9 is still proposed (as a `major`, because it is computed against the same mis-resolved 2.1.3). This rule keys on matchCurrentValue rather than matchPackageNames because Renovate extracts BOTH override scopes as depName 'brace-expansion' with depType 'overrides' and tells them apart only by managerData.parents, which no matcher exposes - so the bare package name cannot select one scope. src/lib/override-hygiene.test.ts asserts this rule still matches the value actually in package.json; without it, editing the override would switch the guard off silently. Lift only when the top-level override itself is no longer needed.

Keep the NESTED minimatch@^3 -> brace-expansion override inside 2.x (#161/#82). minimatch@3.1.5 calls `expand(pattern)` on a default import, and 5.x's CommonJS build exports only `{ expand }`, so forcing 5.x here raises `TypeError: expand is not a function` inside @eslint/config-array and ESLint exits 2 having linted 0 FILES - which a bare 'did lint pass' check reads as success. Forcing minimatch@^10 instead is no better (minimatch@10 is not callable and has no .default, breaking eslint-plugin-react, eslint-plugin-import and eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y), and no release of eslint, @eslint/eslintrc or the three eslint-config-next plugins has moved off minimatch@3, including eslint@10. This copy is reachable only from devDependencies lint tooling. Concretely, this cap is what stops the renovate/brace-expansion-5.x branch - which proposes rewriting THIS entry to ^5.0.0, not the top-level one - from ever landing; the wanted 5.0.8 -> 5.0.9 bump is a different stream (renovate/brace-expansion-5.x-lockfile) against the entry above, and is unaffected. Same accepted trade-off as the typescript cap: allowedVersions also applies to vulnerabilityAlerts MRs, so a 5.x-only advisory fix cannot arrive here automatically - but it could not be applied without breaking the lint toolchain regardless, and this copy is dev-only. The real remediation is minimatch@3 leaving the eslint plugin chain; when it does, delete the override and this rule together.

Cap postgres majors (#161/#17). A postgres major is a dump/restore migration, not an image swap, so it cannot arrive as a routine dependency MR. The pin appears in THREE places that have to move together - docker/docker-compose.prod.yml twice (the `db` service and the `backup` service) and charts/dlectroflow/values.yaml - and the chart's backup dumpImage defaults to postgres.image so that pg_dump stays matched to the server major. Moving one pin without the others makes pg_dump version-mismatch the server it is dumping. Renovate proposes 16 -> 18 across all three today (branch renovate/postgres-18.x). It could never automerge (the rule at the top of this list covers only minor/patch/digest/pin), so the cap is not about blocking a merge - it is about not carrying a permanently undecided MR for work that needs a planned data migration. Raise the ceiling as part of that work, in one commit that moves all three pins, and Renovate will re-propose immediately. Digest refreshes and 16.x minor bumps are unaffected.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Labels only, deliberately - a concurrency limit or schedule set here would be a no-op (#243). Renovate ALWAYS raises a security PR: every limit gate in its branch/PR workers is guarded by `&& !config.isVulnerabilityAlert` and vulnerability upgrades sort ahead of everything else, so `prConcurrentLimit`, `branchConcurrentLimit`, `prHourlyLimit`, `commitHourlyLimit` and `schedule` are all ignored on this path - the docs put it as 'vulnerability alerts skip the line'. src/lib/renovate-hygiene.test.ts fails if one is added back, because renovate-config-validator accepts the key and so cannot tell you it does nothing. Separately, this block is inert on GitLab today: Renovate implements `platform.getVulnerabilityAlerts` on its GitHub platform only, so no advisory source reaches it, and `osvVulnerabilityAlerts` is deliberately left off - see #243 for that reasoning and what enabling it would cost.
